summary: A nested drain/copy counter: levels (b, tail) with b -> about 4.5b, 8b or 2b by residue classes (symbolic level map, no halting case), but two level types run a counter whose outcome depends on the digits of a block length; no halt in 1.6e15 steps.
title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1LC0RB_1LE0LD_0LB1LD_0RA0LF_---0RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_1LC0RB_1LE0LD_0LB1LD_0RA0LF_---0RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The run is a sequence of levels (b, tail); the level map is known symbolically for twelve of the fourteen level types met (trusted code, no halting case), the four cycles it uses are proved in Lean, and the run from blank tape passes nine levels in 1.6 × 1015 steps without halting. Two level types contain a counter, and there the next level depends on the digits of a block length.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 53,968 cells have been visited and 29,068 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.638). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.46).

claims.title: The split cycle
claims.text: 0^∞ B>0 0 (110101)^c 1 1 0 1 (100)^(d+3) 1 0 1 1 1 (01011)^(b+1) 0 1 0^∞ reaches the same with c+1, d+1, b+3 in 32b + 50c + 24d + 228 steps, for every b, c, d.

claims.title: The copy cycle
claims.text: One visit of the right end in the copy phase: L (01111)^(n+2) (010)^(m+1) 0 1111 (00111)^(m+1) B> 0^∞ takes 28m+55 steps and moves one word of the old final block into a new (010) block and a new final block (00111), for every n, m and every tape L on the left.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: c/hsim2.cpp, a block macro simulator that takes a linear jump over k cycles only after checking the cycle symbolically for every larger count (step count summed exactly), runs to 1.05·1015 steps without a halt. At 5·1010 steps its state and every cell agree with plain simulation (py/cmpc.py).

claims.title: The feed round
claims.text: A fourth phase feeds the block (110101)^c back into the final block at about 5.08 words per word, through a small counter of 3-cell digits. One round, for every c, d, b, is a symbolic trace of 32b+34c+24d+3813 steps found by bbtools.symtm; it is too long for the Lean kernel to check in reasonable time and memory, so it is not in Rules.lean.

claims.title: The level sequence
claims.text: Final-block size at each copy, from the accelerated simulator: 13 (5.4·10<sup>3</sup> steps), 108 (2.8·10<sup>5</sup>), 907 (2.0·10<sup>7</sup>), 7,265 (1.26·10<sup>9</sup>), 14,531 after a split (6.1·10<sup>9</sup>), 33,000 (1.67·10<sup>10</sup>), 83,545 (1.66·10<sup>11</sup>), 375,963 (3.37·10<sup>12</sup>), about 3.0·10<sup>6</sup> (2.15·10<sup>14</sup>), about 6.0·10<sup>6</sup> after a split (5.4·10<sup>14</sup>), 6,015,471 (1.05·10<sup>15</sup>). The ratios (about 8, 4.5, 2 at a split) depend on which phase starts, so the level map looks like a Collatz-style map on residues; its exact form is not derived.

claims.title: The pour cycle, visit by visit
claims.text: Twenty one-visit theorems: 0^∞ 1 (100111)^3 (001)^(d+4) 1 1 1 0 (01110)^(a+2) 0 1 1 1 B> 0^∞ returns after 20 visits of the right end with d − 2 and a + 10, for every a and d.

claims.title: The level map for twelve of fourteen level types; no halting case
claims.text: A level starts when the final block has just been rewritten as (01111)^b. A symbolic run with b and the other block counts free (residue splits on demand, every assumption recorded) gives the next level for 89 cases of 14 types, e.g. b = 4k+r → 18k + const on the short tails; no case halts. Two cases fail: the levels with a long block (011110)^m or (110011)^m, where a counter runs between the blocks.

claims.title: No halt in 1.6 × 10<sup>15</sup> steps; nine levels
claims.text: The accelerated simulator (jumps only over symbolically verified cycles; cell-checked against plain simulation at 5 × 10<sup>10</sup> steps) follows the run through levels b = 906, 910, 7,265, 14,531, about 83,546, 375,960, 375,965, 3,007,734 and 6,015,471.

claims.title: No exact growth cycle; counter levels depend on digits
claims.text: The second round of levels repeats the types of the first, but growth is multiplicative and the next type depends on b mod 4 and, after a counter level, on the digits of the counter length m: with b = 400 and m = 1..48 every level reaches a next one without halting, but the new b is not monotone in m.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The level structure is exact for twelve level types and none of their cases halts, but two level types contain a counter whose outcome depends on the digits of a block length, so the set of level types does not close; the machine is Collatz-like with a counter inside.

check: python3 holdouts/1RB1RA_1LC0RB_1LE0LD_0LB1LD_0RA0LF_---0RE/py/cmpc.py 5e10      # hsim2 against plain simulation, cell for cell (about 4 min)
python3 holdouts/1RB1RA_1LC0RB_1LE0LD_0LB1LD_0RA0LF_---0RE/py/closure.py   # level map, about 1 min: 14 types, 89 cases, 2 failed, NOT CLOSED

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. This machine keeps a few long blocks on its tape and works like a nested counter: it pours blocks of 010 into one big block of 01011, a little per sweep, and each time everything is poured it copies the big block back out as new 010 blocks, about eight times larger than the last round.

facts.text: The drain and split cycles, proved in Lean for every block size.
Growth of the final block from one level to the next (13, 108, 907, 7,265).
No halt in the C simulator; 53,968 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.638). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.46).
After 109 steps the tape spans 53,968 cells (8,338 left of the start, 31,625 right), with a density of 1s of 0.539.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Long blocks of 010 and one block of 01011
html: Look at the tape whenever the head is at its left end. Apart from a few cells at the ends, it is made of long runs of three words:

for instance at step 33,886,934: 0 0 1 1 0 1 0 0 1 0 1 1 (010)^888 1 1 1 0 1 0 0 1 0 1 1 (010)^906 1 1 1 (01011)^981 0 1. On a rightward sweep the words appear shifted (001, 00111, 11100), so the same block is seen in different phases of the word, but its length is the same.

sections.heading: Three kinds of phase
html:
phasetapeper cycleproof
drain… (010)^a 1 1 1 (01011)^b 0 1a − 4, b + 14 (16 visits of the left end)Lean, drain
split(110101)^c 1 1 0 1 (100)^d 1 0 1 1 1 (01011)^b 0 1c + 1, d − 2, b + 2 (4 visits)Lean, split
feed(110101)^c 1 1 [small blocks] (010)^e 1 1 1 (01011)^bc − 1, b + about 5; the small blocks between act as a countersimulation

In the drain phase the last (010) block loses a pair every four sweeps while the final block gains 3.5 words (so b grows by 7 cells per 2 pairs eaten). When it is empty, the next (010) block to its left starts draining. When none is left, a long copy phase writes the final block back out as a fresh block of 010 of the same length: at step 1,255,481,375 the tape is (010)^7265 1 1 1 (01011)^7265 0 1.

sections.heading: Levels
html: Each copy starts a new level; drained blocks add 3.5 b per block of length b, so the final block grows by a large factor per level:

At the fourth level the left end changes: the split phase moves half of a block into a new block (110101)^c at the left end (c reached 3,634), and in the feed phase that block is fed back, one word every few sweeps, through a small counter of short (010) blocks. The structure looks recursive: the small blocks repeat, at a small scale, what the long ones do.

The machine halts only on F reading a 0. In every phase seen so far F is entered only from E on a 1, moving left onto cells that are 1s inside the words above; a halt would need a phase boundary to put F next to a 0, which has not happened in 1010 steps.

sections.eyebrow: Where a halt would come from
sections.heading: The one way it could stop
sections.html:
The machine stops only one way: state E reads a 1 whose left neighbour is a 0 (E writes 0, steps left into state F, and F has no move on a 0). That pattern has not appeared in 1015 simulated steps: every phase seen so far keeps those neighbourhoods out of reach. Proving that the phases always follow one another the same way would prove the machine runs forever; that is the missing piece.

At 1.05·1015 steps the whole tape is (011101)^1503867 (001)^6015471 01110 (10110)^6015471: three long blocks, the shape the machine returns to at every level.

sections.heading: Levels: what is known for every block size
html: Call a level the moment the final block has just been rewritten as (01111)^b, with a tail T of other cells to its left. A symbolic run with b left free gives the next level for each kind of tail:

tailnext b
plain (P)b + 4, and a copy (100)^(b−5) joins the tail
with a copy (100)^cabout 4.5 b + 3.5 c (exact formula per residue of b and c mod 4)
five short tailsb = 4k + r → 18k + const (× 4.5); r picks the next tail
doubling tail2b + 1, and a block of m ≈ b/2 six-cell words appears
with (011110)^m or (110011)^mnot known in general: a counter runs between the blocks

None of the 89 cases halts. The last row is why the machine is still open: with b = 400, the lengths m = 13, 14, 15 give b = 2048, 2441, 1862 next, so the result depends on the digits of m and no finite list of shapes covers it. From blank tape the run passes b = 906, 910, 7,265, 14,531, about 83,546, 375,960, 375,965, 3,007,734, 6,015,471 in 1.6 × 1015 steps.
